name: Yuan and Ming blue-and-white porcelain
summary: White porcelain painted in cobalt blue under a clear glaze. Jingdezhen potters made it in the Yuan dynasty and refined it for the Ming court into the best-known ceramic of the world.

philosophy.core_thesis: Cobalt blue painted straight on white porcelain and sealed under a clear glaze gives a lasting picture that cannot rub or fade.
design_principles: Paint cobalt oxide on the dry, unfired body with a soft brush, then dip in a clear glaze.
Fire once at 1280 to 1330 °C in a strong flame, so that the porcelain turns white and dense.
Divide the surface into bands: a main field, a shoulder band, and a foot border of lappets or waves.
In the Yuan style, fill the field with dense bands; in the Ming style, leave more white ground.
Draw dragons, lotus scrolls, phoenixes, flowers and landscapes in outline and wash.
Use a deep blue with dark spots in the early work, and a clean soft blue in the later Ming work.
Write the reign mark in six characters in a ring or a square under the base.
anti_patterns: Brown or red earthenware showing at the foot
Bright overglaze enamels as the main colour
A thick opaque white tin glaze
A grey or cloudy body from a weak firing

form.shape: Large dishes, jars, meiping vases, pear-shaped bottles, moon flasks, bowls and stem cups.
form.profile: A strong, round body with a high shoulder; the profile is full and has a clean, firm curve.
form.foot_and_rim: A neat foot ring that is bare of glaze or has a thin glaze; the rim is thin and often with a brown or blue line.
form.proportion: Dish diameter 35 to 50 cm in the Yuan; jar height 30 to 45 cm; wall 4 to 10 mm, thin for the Ming bowl.
rules: Throw large jars in two parts and join at the waist.
Keep the base of the foot flat and unglazed or lightly glazed.
Run the painting in bands that follow the line of the form.
Place the main scene on the belly and the borders at the shoulder and the foot.

bodies.rule: Use a white, hard porcelain of kaolin and china stone. It must be dense, white and slightly translucent in thin walls.

methods: turning the foot and the wall
forming.joins: Large vases are thrown in two or three parts and joined at the neck; handles and spouts are luted with slip.
forming.details: A clear glaze with a faint blue-green tint, dark spots in early cobalt, and a base mark of the reign in six characters in later pieces.

glaze.pattern: Dragons and waves, lotus scrolls, peonies, phoenixes and landscape scenes in bands; the Ming style leaves more white between motifs.
glaze.gloss: Glassy, about 80 to 95 GU, with a clear, slightly blue-green cast.
glaze.wear: The painting stays stable under the glaze; the glaze may show fine crackle and a small brown rim of iron.

palette.strategy: Cobalt blue on a white ground: a dense dark blue in the Yuan and a soft clear blue in the Ming.

firing.kiln: An egg-shaped kiln at Jingdezhen, fired with pine wood, which holds a lot of saggared pieces.
processes: paint cobalt on the unfired body
firing.scale: The imperial kilns at Jingdezhen employed thousands of potters, and made the ware for the court and for export.
firing.signs: A clear glaze with a blue-green tint, cobalt with dark spots, and a thin white foot with a reign mark.

pieces.form: Large dish with a dragon and clouds and a border of waves
Jar with a high shoulder, floral scrolls and lappets, and a domed lid
Pear-shaped bottle with a long neck and a lotus scroll
Moon flask with two handles and a dense peony pattern

positive: lotus scroll on a round jar
dense Yuan style or open Ming style

evidence.title: Yuan underglaze blue porcelain from Jingdezhen
Ming vase of the Xuande period, 1425–1436
Ming blue-and-white dragon vase, British Museum

emotion.target_response: A crisp, bright calm: the viewer sees a deep blue picture on white and feels order, clarity and old craft.

use_cases: a vase or jar with a blue pattern on white
a museum label on Chinese export and court porcelain
a prompt for a classical Chinese interior
avoid_when: the brief needs bright multicolour enamel
the brief needs a handmade earthenware look

modifiers.how: Change the body to earthenware, cover it with white tin glaze and keep the blue painting.
Keep the white porcelain, reduce the blue, and add overglaze red, green and gold in a spare design.
